A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MuCO study. All 29 pages of v1 and 26 pages of v2, including Appendices A–F, are readable and support comparison of text, equations, tables and figures despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original CPSea experiments measuring cyclization success, energy, diversity, secondary structure and efficiency, with sampling analyses and component ablations in Section 4 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds physicochemical and distributional evaluations, cyclic-encoding and random-initialization controls, and AlphaFold3/ProteinZen comparisons.

M1.justification: The backbone flow model, torsional side-chain flow with Cyclic RPE, topology detection, CHARMM36 refinement and hierarchical sampling remain unchanged. Equations and Algorithms 1–3 retain the same procedures. The new linear-RPE variant is an ablation, not a revision of MuCO.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same CPSea training population and CPTrans, CPBind, CPCore and CPSea-PDB evaluation subsets, with the same peptide-length coverage and cyclization tasks. The added evaluations use the existing CPSea-PDB subset.

E2.justification: Appendix F.2 and Table 15 add evaluated AlphaFold3 and ProteinZen comparators, substantially extending comparison beyond the original AF2-derived and geometric-regression baselines to additional end-to-end methods. The four original quantitative baselines remain, although Figure 5 removes AfCycDesign and WGFormer from its case comparison.

E3.justification: v2 adds hydrogen-bond, radius-of-gyration and SASA deviation/RMSD metrics, plus JS similarity for torsion and secondary-structure distributions. It also introduces linear-versus-cyclic RPE and random-initialization control protocols. Existing data splits, training budgets, sampling configurations and physical-refinement criteria remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 adds two targeted analyses: Table 5 isolates Cyclic RPE's contribution to side-chain fidelity, and Table 6 tests whether CHARMM36 alone can recover secondary structure from random coordinates. These materially extend the retained stage-replacement, refinement and sampling analyses.

E5.justification: The new random-initialization control explicitly reports 20 independent trials and first-sample, average and best-of-20 summaries. This is new repeated-trial reporting, not an increase in runs for the original benchmarks. Confidence intervals and significance tests are not added.

E6.justification: Original table values are retained: v1 Tables 1–10 match v2 Tables 1, 4 and 7–14. New Tables 2, 3, 5, 6 and 15 add substantial results, including MuCO JS similarities of 0.589/0.479/0.852 and secondary-structure gain of 0.2759 versus the random-trial mean of -0.0241. Figure 5 removes AfCycDesign/WGFormer case results.

T1.justification: Appendix D.1 adds a mathematical definition for the newly introduced JS-similarity measure: one minus the averaged KL divergence to the mixture distribution, applied to marginal and joint distributions. The flow objectives, geometric constraints and other existing mathematics remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: three-stage generative cyclization, efficient hierarchical sampling, and advantages in stability, diversity, secondary-structure recovery and efficiency. The new experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 interprets physicochemical agreement as evidence of pharmaceutical relevance, attributes improved torsion fidelity to Cyclic RPE, and strengthens the argument that learned initialization enables structural recovery. Final limitations remain unchanged, but Appendix D.2 drops v1's explanation that some unfiltered CPSea structures can fail closure or force-field criteria.

D1.justification: The abstract newly supplies a MuCO demo repository link, and Section 3.2 identifies the CP-Composer/CPSea open-source pipeline underlying topology detection. Existing architecture details, hyperparameters, hardware, training times, data filtering and refinement settings are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds the ProteinZen citation and comparison, and explicitly acknowledges CP-Composer/CPSea as sources for the topology pipeline. The related-work framework remains stable. CPSea's date and other publication-metadata updates refer to retained works rather than additional research.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section order are retained. v2 makes grammatical and terminology corrections, updates affiliations, revises Appendix D's explanations, and adds acknowledgements, an impact statement and Appendix F.2. These are localized changes rather than a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column layout to a two-column conference-style layout, extensively resizing and repositioning displays. Five tables are added, Figure 5 is reduced from six columns to four, and the sampling table changes from side-by-side dataset panels to vertically grouped rows. Plot labels, legends and captions also receive revisions.

improvement.justification: The new distributional metrics, targeted controls and end-to-end comparisons strengthen validation of the existing method, while the demo link improves access information. The gains are useful but bounded: the additions concentrate on CPSea-PDB, small RPE improvements lack uncertainty estimates, and Table 6's positive best-of-20 random gain qualifies the prose's categorical failure claim. Overall, v2 provides better support with some remaining overinterpretation.
